input.quote: Each Service Option Attachment will renew automatically for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term of the applicable Service Option Attachment unless either party notifies the other party in writing at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term for the applicable Service Option Attachment that it has elected to terminate such Service Option Attachment.
input.rationale: § 3.2 renews each Service Option Attachment automatically but requires ninety (90) days' written notice to stop renewal, exceeding our fallback ceiling of a 60-day non-renewal notice window. We have made the shortest operative cure — the notice period is now 60 days — which lands the clause at the fallback. No provision in the Agreement permits a renewal price increase; Charges are fixed by the Service Option Attachments and Order Forms (§ 4.1), so the conditional 5 percent uplift element is satisfied on the document's own terms. Preferred-only points noted but not redlined: renewal terms track the previous term rather than a 12-month cap, the opt-out is 60 rather than 30 days, and there is no Vendor renewal reminder. Two items for the deal team: the mutual drafting means IBM's non-renewal notice also drops to 60 days, and if any Order Form term exceeds 12 months the roll-forward would create an automatic multi-year renewal, which we should escalate rather than accept.

mappings.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
mappings.quote: Charges for applicable Services will be specified in Service Option Attachments and Order Forms.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have shortened the non-renewal notice window in § 3.2 from ninety days to 60 days so we can exit an automatic renewal within our fallback 60-day window; our preferred position is a 30-day opt-out with a Vendor renewal reminder.
proposal.summary: Shorten non-renewal notice window from 90 days to 60 days in § 3.2.
